newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians begin evacuating Israelis from Nablus.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians begin evacuating Israelis from Nablus.

text.p: Palestinian police began evacuating trapped Israeli soldiers from a West Bank shrine where some of the bloodiest confrontations took place between the two sides on Thursday, witnesses said.

They said Palestinian policemen drove the first group of 42 Israeli soldiers from the traditional tomb of the biblical Joseph in Palestinian-ruled Nablus where they had been besieged by Palestinian demonstrators.

"The first group left in three vehicles. Three officers rode with the Palestinian governor of Nablus," one witness said. The tomb is an island in the city of 130,000 Palestinians under self-rule since late last year.

It was not clear how many soldiers had left and when the rest would leave. Under a peace deal with Israel that expanded Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank, the site is supposed to remain in Israeli hands.

A senior Palestinian security source said six Israeli soldiers were killed and 12 others were wounded when PLO security forces and Palestinian demonstrators overran the site. An Israeli general said Palestinian police had fired on the tomb.
Dead and wounded soldiers were the first to be evacuated in Palestinian ambulances. Demonstrators burned eight Israeli military vehicles when they overran the site.
